units.name: Prediction-based scoring model
units.summary: Understanding is measured by graded prediction answers per unit and developer, decayed by weighted commit mass, and turned into importance-weighted debt.
units.decision: Measure by quiz evidence (1/0.5/0/-0.5), decay 0.9 per weighted commit landed on the unit, weak capped prior from own commits, debt = importance*(1-understanding), team view via bus factor; pure functions with no I/O.
units.alternatives: Provenance-only (who typed it) scoring; time-based decay; self-reported understanding.
units.why: BRIEFING argues provenance says nothing at the architectural level in AI-driven workflows, so prediction tests the actual mental model; math in a pure module is easy to test.

units.name: Architectural map and unit hierarchy
units.summary: Builds a two-level map of decisions/modules/boundaries/flows from structural clusters, history candidates and an LLM, then attaches churn, importance and provenance.
units.decision: Units are LLM-proposed architectural units (not files), stored as a versioned (v3) hierarchy with ids parent/child, capped in number, and rescorable without the LLM.
units.alternatives: File- or directory-level units; purely algorithmic clustering; flat unit list.
units.why: Package internals are out of scope by design and only architectural understanding counts as debt.

units.name: LLM backend via claude CLI and prompts
units.summary: All LLM use goes through an LLM protocol that shells out to the claude CLI with read-only tools and JSON schemas, with a FakeLLM for offline tests.
units.decision: Subprocess the subscription-billed claude CLI with --json-schema and Read/Glob/Grep only; prompts begin with a TASK: marker that FakeLLM keys on; UDEBT_LLM=fake selects the fake.
units.alternatives: Anthropic API SDK with an API key; no tool access; mocking per test.
units.why: No API key or billing setup, and LLM can verify claims against code; fake keeps tests deterministic.

units.name: JSON persistence under .udebt/
units.summary: All state lives as committed JSON files in .udebt/: shared map, per-developer append-only records, commit weights, responsibility, config.
units.decision: File-based JSON in the repo, one jsonl file per developer so merges are conflict-free, committed by default.
units.alternatives: A database; local-only untracked state; hosted store.
units.why: Team sharing through git with no merge conflicts and no server; hosted is deferred to a later phase.

units.name: CLI command surface
units.summary: The argparse CLI (init, clusters, map, units, responsibility, scope, quiz, status, risk, dig) orchestrates every flow and resolves repo, identity and LLM.
units.decision: One large cli.py module with subcommands as the only public interface, advisory outputs, optional --strict exit codes.
units.alternatives: Library API; per-command modules; editor/Claude Code hook integration.
units.why: Standalone CLI product over git is the stated scope; hooks are a non-goal for now.

units.name: Quiz and dig flow
units.summary: Pick the highest-debt units, generate verified prediction questions, grade free-text answers with the LLM, and append evidence records; dig walks the worst unit.
units.decision: Five questions per session, misconceptions score negative, blank answers are no-penalty known unknowns, graded against the code by the LLM.
units.alternatives: Multiple choice quizzes; static question bank; penalising blanks.
units.why: Confident wrong beliefs are the real hazard; short sessions can be run often.

units.name: Commit provenance and history mining
units.summary: Classifies commits as ai, assisted or human from configurable signatures, loads git history, and mines decision-bearing commits.
units.decision: Signatures are data in config; three commit classes; cheap git heuristics (founding, dependencies, infra, renames) select candidate decision commits for the LLM.
units.alternatives: Hardcoded Claude detection; LLM-only history reading; ignoring provenance.
units.why: Mixed human/AI repos are the primary target and other agents will be added later.

units.name: Commit weight model
units.summary: Each commit gets a weight in [0,1] from heuristics, optionally LLM-refined for the heaviest, cached in .udebt/commits.json, and split across units by line share.
units.decision: Every former commit count (churn, decay, provenance, prior) is weighted mass; the top 40 commits are LLM-classified.
units.alternatives: Raw commit counts; LLM weighting of all commits.
units.why: Reformats and lockfile bumps should not create debt; refinement cost is paid once through caching.

units.name: Structural cluster discovery
units.summary: Builds import and co-change graphs and partitions them with Louvain into candidate clusters fed to the map prompt.
units.decision: Merge import and weighted co-change graphs, ignore huge commits, cluster only code files, attach docs/config afterwards; stdlib-only implementation.
units.alternatives: LLM-only discovery; directory layout as units; third-party graph libraries.
units.why: Gives the LLM grounded structure and keeps runtime dependencies at zero.

units.name: Change risk and advisory gating
units.summary: Scores a change's weight per unit against the author's understanding and reports OUTSIDE/HIGH/CAUTION/OK, usable in a warn-only pre-push hook.
units.decision: Risk is the min over touched units with sqrt line share; signals are advisory, only --strict gives non-zero exit.
units.why: Owner decided gating stays advisory with opt-in soft block; a change is as risky as the unit least understood.

units.name: Responsibility sets and contributor labels
units.summary: Defines which units each developer is expected to understand (CODEOWNERS, footprint, manual) and labels contributors as AI, Joint, Human or Bot.
units.decision: Seeded sets curated by leads with per-developer scope overrides; AI-likelihood labels from metadata only and display-only.
units.alternatives: Everyone responsible for everything; authorship-based scoring.
units.why: Owner answers: repo owners assign roles, metadata-only heuristics; avoids penalising people for units they were never expected to know.

units.name: Briefing and change log discipline
units.summary: BRIEFING.md, CHANGES.md and CLAUDE.md hold scope, decisions and agent instructions that agents must keep in sync with code and README math.
units.decision: Decisions are recorded in docs read and appended by agents, and scoring changes must update the README table alongside.
units.why: Agents build most of the code, so intent needs to be written where they read it.
